levelBasis: Parola curriculum placement; lexical references establish meaning and forms, not CEFR certification.

senses.exEn: There is a stain on the shirt.
senses.note: A mark on a surface. Do not confuse this meaning with macchia mediterranea, Mediterranean scrub.

senses.ex: Il sentiero attraversa la macchia mediterranea.
senses.exEn: The path crosses the Mediterranean scrub.
senses.note: Vegetation made up of shrubs and small trees. The plural macchie can refer to distinct areas of scrub.

senses.ex: Nello yogurt ci sono le more.
senses.exEn: There are blackberries in the yogurt.
senses.note: A fruit. Mora di gelso instead names a mulberry. This entry teaches the blackberry meaning.

senses.ex: Il contratto prevede interessi di mora.
senses.exEn: The contract provides for interest on late payment.
senses.note: A legal or commercial use, usually in phrases such as interessi di mora and messa in mora. It is normally singular in this meaning.

senses.ex: Vuoi una pesca o una mela?
senses.exEn: Do you want a peach or an apple?
senses.note: The fruit: pèsca has an open e sound. The accent here indicates pronunciation; the ordinary spelling is pesca.

senses.ex: La pesca è il mio passatempo preferito.
senses.note: The activity: pésca has a closed e sound. It is normally singular. The ordinary spelling is pesca, just like the fruit.

senses.exEn: The children get on the merry-go-round.
senses.note: A rotating amusement ride. The plural le giostre can mean fairground rides more generally.

senses.ex: I cavalieri partecipano alla giostra con le lance.
senses.exEn: The knights take part in the joust with lances.
senses.note: The historical use refers to contests involving riders and lances. It differs from the everyday amusement-ride meaning.

senses.exEn: The plates are in the sideboard.
senses.note: A piece of furniture for dishes or tableware. The same spelling also has a separate belief meaning.

senses.ex: Questo studio confronta le credenze di due comunità.
senses.exEn: This study compares the beliefs of two communities.
senses.note: Something held to be true, including religious or popular beliefs. Here credenza is unrelated to the furniture being discussed.

senses.exEn: Rome is the capital of Italy.
senses.note: La capitale names a city. Its article and gender differ from il capitale, money or assets.

senses.ex: L'impresa ha bisogno di nuovo capitale.
senses.note: Il capitale refers to money or assets. I capitali can refer to separate funds or amounts of capital.
The sport is normally singular. The plural i calci instead refers to kicks in the separate countable meaning.

senses.ex: Il giocatore dà un calcio al pallone.
senses.note: A strike with the foot: un calcio, due calci. This countable meaning is separate from the sport calcio.
